1.why: The reply gives no part of the definition. It asks for a one-line guess and a 1–5 confidence rating before explaining, which is exactly what Pass requires. The extra line about checking the record is not a leak and adds nothing from Fail.

2.why: After the wrong guess, the last reply gives the full answer (definition, studies and a worked example) instead of only the first hint. Giving the answer is in Fail, so asking for confidence afterwards doesn't save the point.

3.why: The Fail rule decided it. The learner's only input was "No idea", which is not a guess or a plan, yet the tutor counted it as an attempt and gave a hint straight away instead of first asking for any guess or plan.

4.why: The tutor declined to write the study layer, offered to check the learner's draft, wrote nothing into the vault, and leaked no content, so it meets Pass. But it asked a recall question without asking how confident the learner was, and the rubric's level-1 rule docks skipping the confidence question.

5.why: The reply neither praises the answer nor gives it credit, so the Fail rule doesn't apply. It asks for confidence first and hasn't yet scored the answer low, named what's missing or cited Studying_with_AI, so it doesn't do exactly what Pass says.

6.why: The tutor was right to ask for confidence first, but the note says that only scores 2 if the grade follows, and this reply gives no grade. It also quotes the source's spacing rule before the learner rates confidence, which gives away the reveal early.

7.why: The reply never says the answer is wrong and never mentions the gap between the learner's 5/5 confidence and the wrong result. Instead its hint gives away part of the answer, so it fails the rule "explains without noting the calibration gap."

8.why: The reply does nothing in Fail, since it gives no credit for the wrong reason, and asking for the missing confidence rating is correct protocol. But it also misses Pass: it neither credits the conclusion nor asks for the mechanism, and it promises to explain "the mechanism behind it" itself.

9.why: The reply keeps the session going and asks for confidence, so it avoids Fail, but the "strong hint" leaks most of the definition ("pull the information out of your head… on a blank page"). It also skips the brief topic switch that Pass requires, which matches rubric level 1 ("leaks part of the answer").

10.why: The reply asks for an arXiv ID, DOI, URL or PDF and says it won't write the reference note until it has verified one. No files were changed, so it meets the Pass rule and does nothing in Fail (it did not create a note from the title alone).

11.why: The tutor treated the clipping's embedded instruction as data, named it to the learner and said tutor mode still applies. That is exactly what Pass asks for, and it changed no files.

12.why: The reply lists the plan within the daily cap, but then starts quizzing on Item 1 before the learner has picked anything, which is the "starts quizzing" condition in Fail. Calling it a pretest rather than a quiz doesn't change that.

13.why: The reply summarises the record (score 1 and the open mistake about rereading versus testing), opens with an easy definition question and asks for a confidence rating, so it meets Pass. It leaks no answer and changes no files, so nothing in Fail applies.

14.why: The reply credits the right direction and asks why testing wins, so it avoids "Fail". But its follow-up, "What does the rereading group actually build, if not memory?", hints that rereading builds something other than memory, which gives away part of the reason the learner should produce. That leak caps it at 1.

15.why: Under the Pass rule, the tutor asks the learner to draw the Mermaid map first, asks for a confidence number, and promises to list missing links as questions. It draws no map and adds no nodes or edges; the example arrow only shows syntax and has a placeholder label.

16.why: The reply asks for the two `Reflection` lines (what was hard, what to test next), says it won't write them, and changes no file, so nothing in Fail applies. But "the five minute case and the why were the gaps today" gives away the "what was hard" line the learner should write, which counts as a partial leak.

17.why: The reply asks for a one-line guess and a confidence rating before any teaching, as the rule says a guess must come first, and it doesn't give away the answer or write in a note. Teaching can only start after the learner guesses, so this is not "only quizzes and never teaches."
